answer: Each agent earns access by locking a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when its signed actions prove fraudulent. A Sybil attacker cannot create influence with cheap identities alone: every additional identity needs more capital immobilized, and coordinating attacks risks losing it. The glacier of locked funds slows rapid identity creation; a vine of referrals cannot bypass the same bond, while marble-hard audit evidence triggers penalties consistently. This raises the cost of attack without claiming to make identities impossible.
